content: Hey, what are your thoughts on adding open conjectures and problems from the field of Combinatorial Game Theory?
Do you have any examples you could share, to get a better idea of what these typically entail?

An open conjecture that is present is the Periodicity Conjecture for Misère Octal Games where For every finite octal game, the sequence of misère quotient elements [0], [1], [2], ... is eventually periodic.

Some literature regarding this open conjecture and literature related to this problem can be found here: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0612616
Some math theory that could be helpful is https://vihdzp.github.io/combinatorial-games/CombinatorialGames/Nimber/Basic.html , for Nim which i believe can be a Misere octal game.
I appreciate the website link. But, I can't seem to access it as it is giving a 404 error. Can you resend the link to me again?
We don't yet have octal games or misère quotients in the CGT repo, but they're both definitely in scope!
Presumably we could try formalizing them in the CGT repository, then make a PR to the conjectures repo with only the bits and pieces needed to state the conjecture?

I know of another game theory conjecture: the birthday of the product of two surreal numbers is at most the natural product of their birthdays. We actually have a proof-wanted in CGT with this exact statement.

Violeta Hernández said:

Presumably we could try formalizing them in the CGT repository, then make a PR to the conjectures repo with only the bits and pieces needed to state the conjecture?

This would be the best way to add them to the Formal Conjectures Repo indeed. It means duplicating definitions in FormalConjecturesForMathlib but taking the CGT Repo as a dependency would be more of a hassle I suppose.
Sounds good to me! Looking forward to drafting issues and formalizations of these concepts in the repo!
We have a #combinatorial-games channel btw, I'd love to draft out what these concepts look like in Lean
Such PRs to formal-conjectures would be very welcome!
